title: The API Client Access Policy: rules that allow or block a client's resources within time frames

prose.text: Beyond the resources a client holds, a tenant can limit when a client may use them. {{purpose}}

prose.label: Who and where.
prose.text: {{full-permission}} The contract has no access-policy operation, so rules are managed in the console only: [[zidentity.api:no-token-or-policy-paths]].

checks.do: For a client that fails only at certain times or for certain products, whether an access policy rule is assigned to it, and its criteria and action.
After a rule assigned to a client was edited, whether the client is using a newly issued token.

purpose.statement: API client access policies determine an API client's access to specific API resources within set time frames; administrators define the rules and assign them to API clients.

quotes: The API client access policies determine the API client's access to specific API resources within set time frames.
Administrators can define the policy rules and assign them to the required API clients to prevent unauthorized activity and control access to API resources.

criteria-time-resources.statement: A rule's criteria are Time (a repeating behavior, start and end date and time, and a time zone) and Resources (the API resources, that is the scope per Zscaler service); when both are set, the rule applies either one (Any) or both (All).

quotes: Select Any from the drop-down menu to apply either Time or Resources criteria or select All to apply both (Time and Resources) criteria.
Select the repeating behavior for the rule.
Select a start date and time. The rule is valid from this date and time.
Select an end date and time. The rule ends on this date and time.
Select the time zone in which the rule should be valid.
Select the API resources that determine the permissions (scope) the API client has to access the API resources of each Zscaler service.
Criteria: The API resources and time parameters defined in the policy rule.

action-and-status.statement: A rule's action is Allow or Block, and its status is Active or Expired.

quotes: Rule Action: The action (Allow or Block) that is defined for the policy rule.
Rule Status: The status (Active or Expired) of the policy rule.

one-rule-per-client.statement: Only one policy rule can be assigned to an API client at a time.

quotes: Only one policy rule can be assigned to an API client at a time.

full-permission.statement: Authentication Service administrators with Full permission on the API clients and API resources modules can configure a rule; rules are added under Administration > API > API Client Access Policy.

quotes: Authentication Service administrators assigned with Full permission to access the API clients and API resources modules can configure an API client access policy rule.
Go to Administration > API > API Client Access Policy.

edit-updates-token.statement: Editing a rule that is assigned to an API client also updates that client's access token, and the client has to use a valid token.

quotes: If you update the policy rule that is associated with the API client, then the access token is also updated. Ensure to use a valid access token.

no-delete-while-assigned.statement: A rule cannot be deleted while any API client is associated with it.

quotes: You cannot delete the policy rule if any API client is associated with it.
